title: How to Confirm Phone Number Ownership with Lookup Identity Match in Python
summary: Send details like name, address, or date of birth and the Identity Match API will tell you if they match a provided phone number. Reduce fraud and verify identities quickly.
body_markdown:
Time to read: - - - - - August 28, 2026 **Written by**[Kelley Robinson](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/authors/author.krobinson) Twilion [Dylan Frankcom](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/authors/author.dylan-frankcom) Twilion --- ## How to Confirm Phone Number Ownership with Lookup Identity Match in Python Identity Match for phone numbers in the United States and Brazil doesn't require carrier registration and approval. Phone numbers from Canada, France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Spain, and the United Kingdom require[additional carrier registration and approval](https://twlo.my.salesforce-sites.com/countrycarrier/SN_CarrierRegistration_VFP) . Learn more about the[carrier approval process here](https://help.twilio.com/articles/14968525856923-API-Onboarding-Guide-Verify-SNA-Lookup-Identity-Match-Lookup-SIM-Swap-and-More) . There's a lot you can learn from a phone number.[Lookup Identity Match](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match) uses phone numbers as an identity to provide a zero-knowledge match against authoritative data sources like mobile carrier records. This allows you to build real-time confirmation that you're interacting with a real person linked to the phone number provided. Use Identity Match to prevent fake accounts and improve trust with legitimate, unique users. Customers can use Identity Match at sign up, login, and even during account changes or checkout. Best of all, Identity Match happens seamlessly in the background, with lower costs and friction than alternatives like credit bureau and document verification used to satisfy[Anti-Money Laundering](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/key-topics/aml) (AML) rules. This blog post will show you how to use Twilio Lookup Identity Match to confirm phone number ownership and reduce sign up fraud. Here's a sneak peak at what the Identity Match request looks like. Learn more about[accepted parameters](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match#query-parameters) and[coverage](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match#coverage) in the documentation. Copy code ```text curl -X GET "https://lookups.twilio.com/v2/PhoneNumbers/+14159929960\ ?Fields=identity_match\ &FirstName=Jane\ &LastName=Doe\ &AddressLine1=321+Main+Street\ &City=Kingston\ &State=NY\ &PostalCode=12401\ &AddressCountryCode=US\ &DateOfBirth=19860414" \ -u $TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID:$TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN ``` ## Programming Language Support This tutorial is geared towards Python developers, but you can find other languages below: - [JavaScript](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/confirm-phone-number-ownership-lookup-identity-match) ## Prerequisites To code along with this post you'll need: 1. A Twilio account.[Sign up](https://www.twilio.com/try-twilio) or[sign in](https://www.twilio.com/console) . 2. [Submit this form for Identity Match approval](https://twlo.my.salesforce-sites.com/countrycarrier/SN_CarrierRegistration_VFP) (Outside the US and Brazil only; takes[2-4 weeks](https://help.twilio.com/articles/14968525856923-API-Onboarding-Guide-Verify-SNA-Lookup-Identity-Match-Lookup-SIM-Swap-and-More) ) 3. Python 3.14 ([download](https://www.python.org/downloads/) ) 4. pip ## Build the app This post builds a simple Flask application with a phone number input form as a starting point, but you could use your own sign up form instead. The base form relies on the excellent[intl-tel-input](https://intl-tel-input.com/) plugin for collecting phone numbers in[E.164 format](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-e164) . **[You can find the source code on GitHub.](https://github.com/twilio-samples/lookup-identity-match-python)** ### Step 1: Set up the base project Create a new project directory: Copy code ```text mkdir identity-match && cd identity-match ``` Create a` requirements.txt` file: Copy code ```text flask==3.1.3 twilio==9.11.0 python-dotenv==1.2.3 ``` Create and activate a virtual environment: Copy code ```text python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate ``` Install the dependencies: Copy code ```text pip install -r requirements.txt ``` Create a` .env` file and add your Twilio Account SID and Auth Token; you can find both on the front page of your[Twilio Console](https://console.twilio.com/) : Copy code ```text TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID=your_account_sid_here TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN=your_auth_token_here ``` Create` app.py` with the following: Copy code ```text import os from dotenv import load_dotenv from flask import Flask, jsonify, request, send_from_directory from twilio.rest import Client load_dotenv() app = Flask(__name__, static_folder="static") @app.route("/") def index(): return send_from_directory("static", "index.html") @app.route("/lookup", methods=["POST"]) def lookup(): phone = request.form.get("phone", "") if not phone: return jsonify({"success": False, "error": "Missing parameter; please provide a phone number."}), 400 try: client = Client(os.environ["TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID"], os.environ["TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN"]) result = client.lookups.v2.phone_numbers(phone).fetch() success = result.valid if not success: raise ValueError(f"Invalid phone number {phone}: {result.validation_errors}") return jsonify({"success": True}) except Exception as e: return jsonify({"success": False, "error": str(e)}), 400 if __name__ == "__main__": app.run(debug=True) ``` Create a` static` directory and add` static/index.html` : Copy code ```text International Telephone Input

International Telephone Input

Validate phone numbers with automatic country detection and the Twilio Lookup API

Try it out

``` Also download` static/styles.css` from the[completed project on GitHub](https://github.com/twilio-samples/lookup-identity-match-python) and save it to your` static` directory. Test out the project by running` flask run` , you should be able to open[http://localhost:5000](http://localhost:5000/) and see a phone number input form. ### Step 2: Extend your sign up form with Identity Match Identity match needs information about the phone number owner to match against.[Parameters](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match#query-parameters) can be any combination of name, address, national ID or date of birth. This example is going to use first and last name, so you need to start by making sure your form has fields to collect those separately: Open *static/index.html* file and replace everything inside the`
` tags with the following: Copy code ```text
``` This adds a first name and last name input in addition to the phone number input. Further down in *index.html* in the script section, add the following code under` const data = …` to extract the name input values. Copy code ```text data.append("firstName", document.getElementById("firstName").value); data.append("lastName", document.getElementById("lastName").value); ``` Then, head over to *app.py* file to make use of the data and call the Lookup Identity Match API. The existing code already calls the basic Lookup API for formatting and validation, so you need to add the additional data parameters to tell the API to use the Identity Match package. Add` first_name` and` last_name` to the form data extraction after the` phone` variable: Copy code ```text first_name = request.form.get("firstName", "") last_name = request.form.get("lastName", "") ``` Then, update the` .fetch()` call to pass the Identity Match fields: Copy code ```text result = client.lookups.v2.phone_numbers(phone).fetch( fields="identity_match", first_name=first_name, last_name=last_name, ) ``` ### Step 3: Interpret the results of a Lookup Identity Match response After calling the Lookup API, you need to decide what to do with the[information in the response](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match#response-properties) . Here's what the identity match portion of a sample response looks like: Copy code ```text { "first_name_match": "exact_match", "last_name_match": "high_partial_match", "address_lines_match": "no_match", "city_match": "no_match", "state_match": "high_partial_match", "postal_code_match": "no_data_available", "address_country_match": "exact_match", "national_id_match": null, "date_of_birth_match": "exact_match", "summary_score": 90, "error_code": null, "error_message": null }, ``` Possible responses include` exact_match` ,` no_match` , and` no_data_available` . Name and address fields also support partial matches. Learn more about[match scores in the documentation](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/identity-match#match-scores) . The API will respond` null` if you don't provide an input to match on. This application is only looking at name matches and will consider the match a success if it's an exact match or high partial match (e.g. Kelly instead of Kelley – happens all the time). Back in *app.py,* replace` success = result.valid` and the` if not success` block with the following: Copy code ```text fnm = result.identity_match.get("first_name_match") lnm = result.identity_match.get("last_name_match") match_values = ("exact_match", "high_partial_match") success = ( result.valid and fnm in match_values and lnm in match_values ) resp_body = { "success": success, "msg": f"First name is {fnm}. Last name is {lnm}", } ``` Then replace` return jsonify({"success": True})` with: Copy code ```text return jsonify(resp_body) ``` Finally, make two small changes to display the response message in the *index.html* file. Replace the inside of the` if (json.success) {` block with: Copy code ```text info.style.display = ""; info.innerHTML = json.msg; ``` And since you're no longer only checking the phone number, update the error message line (` error.innerHTML` ) in the` else` block a few lines below: Copy code ```text error.innerHTML = "Cannot register with the information provided. Please ensure you're using a phone number you own." ``` ## Run the application Navigate back to your terminal, and restart the application with` flask run` (enter` CTRL + C` first if it's still running). Now head back over to[http://localhost:5000](http://localhost:5000/) and test it out!! ## Next steps for identity verification You can extend your application with other Lookup packages like[Line Type Intelligence](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/v2-api/line-type-intelligence) ,[SIM swap detection](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/lookup-sim-swap) and more. Check out our[documentation to learn more about what's possible with the Lookup API](https://www.twilio.com/docs/lookup/api) . Another way to prevent invalid phone numbers is to do[phone verification - we also have an API for that](https://www.twilio.com/docs/verify) ! I can't wait to see what you build and secure.
